concepts.quote: If you compile after every few lines, each error is next to the code you just wrote, so it is easy to find.
concepts.why: States the general strategy of compiling often while making small changes so each error is found close to its cause, reasoning beyond the given one-shot compile.

concepts.quote: compile after every few lines, each error is next to the code you just wrote
concepts.why: Identifies the broken rule (compile after each small change) and explains why the 200-lines-then-compile scenario makes errors hard to trace, via a counterfactual change to the strategy.
The answer says nothing about reading or interpreting the error messages themselves.
Implicitly treats the errors as caught at compile time but states nothing more about them.
